title: Same place, same belief: each member's tile-belief map for one place must agree across the three survey photographs (Jensen-Shannon consistency, AugMix-style), trained on batches that hold every place in all three surveys
hypothesis: Champion exp 20 (0.0777) on held-out truedop_2024: usable 93.0%, false 0.75% (3 frames), abstain 6.25% (25 frames); the three training photographs score 100% usable / 0% false at the same held-out viewpoints. So what remains is purely the survey gap, and it is mostly ABSTENTION: on a foreign photograph a member's belief spreads off the right 3x3 block (min-member block mass < 0.3). The run's own clean diagnostic shows the same gap INSIDE training: on 512 fixed clean training-lattice places, each member's argmax tile agrees across the three training surveys only 84% of the time (xsurvey_agree [0.844, 0.844]) while per-survey clean top1 is ~0.88-0.91 — i.e. the loss never asks a member to hold the SAME belief about a place in two photographs; it asks each photograph separately to hit the label, and CE is satisfied by survey-specific routes to it, with survey-specific confidence. Two facts about the code make this sharper than it looks: (1) the cross-entropy cannot see agreement at all, and (2) although chunks are 'paired' (every position in all three surveys), run_epoch draws each 64-view mini-batch by a random permutation of the 4,095-view chunk, so the three survey views of a place almost never meet in one gradient step. Every earlier attempt at cross-survey invariance acted on the FEATURE (exp 3: cosine of GAP features, from scratch, reverted; exp 9: within-place variance penalty, crashed at 1e9, never measured; exp 8: DINOv2 distillation, from scratch, reverted), before the pretrained trunk existed and never on the thing the confidence gate actually reads. This experiment acts on the OUTPUT: the belief distribution over 2,970 tiles. Following AugMix (Hendrycks et al., ICLR 2020), whose Jensen-Shannon consistency across augmented views is the component that most improved accuracy AND calibration under distribution shift, each member's deployed softmax for one place in the three surveys is pulled toward their mixture. A member that already knows the place in two surveys gets a gradient telling its third view to put its belief in the same place with the same sharpness — exactly the behaviour an abstaining 2024 frame lacks. Since the photometric augmentation is drawn independently per view, the term also asks for agreement across re-photographing nuisances. Builds on exp 2 (paired-survey batches, kept) by finally making the pairing reach the gradient, and on exps 3/9 by moving their invariance goal from feature space to belief space on today's pretrained trunk. Architecture, graph, decode, committee, MixStyle, margin loss, augmentation, schedule and weight averaging all unchanged; the members stay independent (no cross-member term).
method: model/train.py only. (a) Mini-batches are built from whole PLACES: permute the chunk's positions, take P = BATCH_SIZE // n_caps = 21 positions per batch and all n_caps = 3 survey views of each (63 views, survey-grouped), instead of a random permutation of views. (b) Per member, add LAMBDA_JSD * JSD where JSD = mean over places of (1/K) sum_k KL(p_k || pbar), p_k = softmax(COS_SCALE * cos) (the deployed, margin-free belief) of the place's view in survey k, pbar = mean_k p_k. LAMBDA_JSD = 6.0. Same grouping in the BN recalibration pass. Nothing else changes.
expected_outcome: Predicted on truedop_2024: mission 0.078 -> ~0.050-0.070; usable_fix_rate 93.0% -> ~94-95.5%, gained mainly from abstentions (6.25% -> ~4-5%) whose min-member block mass rises above 0.3 because a member's belief on a new survey is now trained to be as sharp, in the same place, as on the others; false_fix_rate at or below 0.75% (the consistency term also penalises one survey's confident-elsewhere belief, so it should not rise). train_capture_diagnostics stay ~100% usable. Training-log signals: the clean survey diagnostic xsurvey_agree should rise from 0.844 toward >=0.9 and the logged per-epoch jsd should fall well below its epoch-1 value; xs_cos_same should rise modestly. Refutation: 2024 usable flat or down with xsurvey_agree clearly up means agreement among the three training surveys does not transfer to the fourth (the abstentions are about content the three never show, e.g. 2024-only construction), and the next lever is data/views rather than invariance. If xsurvey_agree does not rise, the term was too weak or overpowered by CE and the hypothesis is untested at this weight. A drop in usable together with lower mean_max_softmax means the term smoothed beliefs (over-regularised) rather than aligning them.
init_strategy: pretrained:efficientnet_b0 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..7] (torchvision, Apache-2.0 weights), fine-tuned at 0.1x LR
eli5: The model learns Berlin from three different aerial photographs taken in different years and seasons. Until now it was graded on each photograph separately, so it could recognise a street corner in one photo with total certainty and only half-heartedly in another, and nobody minded. Now, every time it studies a place, it sees that place in all three photographs at once and is also marked down whenever its three answers disagree — so it learns to be equally sure about a place whatever photograph it is looking at, which is what it needs when the drone's own camera shows it a fourth.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: the 128 px frame is enlarged to 224 px and read by two independent copies of EfficientNet-B0 (pre-trained on ImageNet, Apache-2.0), fine-tuned on Berlin; each reads a 112-channel 14×14 map and a 320-channel 7×7 map, each lifted to 56 numbers and averaged over the frame into a 112-number place description; the weights carried are the average of the many versions visited over the second half of training

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor's description is centred, scaled to unit length and compared by angle against one unit-length reference direction per map tile (~3,000 tiles, 128 m each); the angle match times a fixed sharpness (30) is the tile score. The two members' tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: same place, same belief. Every training batch now holds 21 places, each seen in all three survey photographs (each view with its own random re-photographing), and besides being graded on the right tile, each member is penalised (Jensen-Shannon divergence, weight 6) whenever its belief maps for one place in the three photographs differ — in where they point or in how sure they are. Everything else as before: cross-survey style mixing, angular-margin tile loss, offset loss, pre-trained blocks at a tenth of the learning rate, 8 epochs, the average of the second half's weights is what flies

implementation_brief:
Edit model/train.py ONLY. model/model.py is untouched (graph, parameter count, ONNX export, loss_fn identical to experiment 20).

1. Constants next to AVG_EVERY: `LAMBDA_JSD = 6.0  # weight of the per-member cross-survey Jensen-Shannon consistency term` . Keep BATCH_SIZE = 64 as the nominal size; derive `places_per_batch = max(1, BATCH_SIZE // n_caps)` (21 for 3 captures -> 63 views).

2. Survey-grouped batching. chunk_views() already orders views POSITION-MAJOR: view j = position (j // n_caps), capture (j % n_caps), all K captures of a position share one heading. In run_epoch(), replace `perm = torch.randperm(n).to(device)` / `for i in range(0, n, BATCH_SIZE): idx = perm[i:i+BATCH_SIZE]` with: `n_pos = n // n_caps`; `pperm = torch.randperm(n_pos, device=device)`; loop `for i in range(0, n_pos, places_per_batch)`: `pidx = pperm[i:i+places_per_batch]`; `idx = (pidx.unsqueeze(1) * n_caps + torch.arange(n_caps, device=device)).reshape(-1)` (so the batch is [P*K] views, place-major, the K views of each place contiguous). B = len(idx). Everything downstream (gpu_crops, soft targets, per-member independent augment_views draw, autocast, residual offset target, loss_fn, statistics) is unchanged and operates on these idx. Assert once per run (outside the step loop, e.g. in train_area or on the first chunk using CPU tensors) that n % n_caps == 0 and that cap_idx of a chunk equals arange(n_caps).repeat(n_pos) so the grouping assumption is checked rather than trusted. Apply the SAME grouped batching in recalibrate_bn() (its own randperm loop), so BN statistics are re-measured on batches composed like the training ones; keep its n_batches counting per batch.

3. JSD term, per member, inside the existing member loop right after `logits_k = COS_SCALE * cos_k`: `P = B // n_caps`; `logp = F.log_softmax(logits_k, dim=1).view(P, n_caps, -1)`; `p = logp.exp()`; `log_m = p.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-7).log()`; `jsd_k = (p * (logp - log_m)).sum(dim=2).mean()` (mean over places and captures = (1/K) sum_k KL(p_k || pbar), averaged over places); `loss = loss + loss_fn(cos_k, off_k, soft_t, off_t_k) + LAMBDA_JSD * jsd_k`. All in float32 (cos_k is already .float()). Use the margin-free deployed logits (COS_SCALE * cos_k), NOT loss_fn's margin logits. No cross-member term: members stay independent. Gradients flow through all K views (no detach of the mixture), as in AugMix. Accumulate an on-device `jsd_sum += jsd_k.detach() * B / N_MEMBERS` (no .item() in the loop) and return it as "jsd_sum" in run_epoch's stats dict; loss_sum keeps including the JSD term.

4. Logging/metrics: add `jsd={stats['jsd_sum']/max(seen,1):.4f}` to the per-epoch log line. In the returned metrics dict keep every existing key and add "lambda_jsd": LAMBDA_JSD, "places_per_batch": places_per_batch, "batch_views": places_per_batch * n_caps, "final_jsd" (last epoch's mean). Append ", survey-grouped batches (21 places x all 3 surveys), per-member cross-survey Jensen-Shannon belief consistency (lambda 6.0)" to "capture_sampling". The survey_diag function and its xsurvey_agree / xs_cos_same / clean_top1 outputs stay exactly as they are (they are the read-outs for this hypothesis).

5. Add a short 'CROSS-SURVEY BELIEF CONSISTENCY (experiment 23)' paragraph to the train.py module docstring, in the style of the existing per-experiment paragraphs, describing the grouped batching and the JSD term.

Contracts to preserve (the frozen scorer depends on them): train.py CLI unchanged — `python -m model.train --area berlin --out-dir runs/<id> [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket K] [--seed S]`, writing <out-dir>/models/<area>.onnx; the ONNX contract in model/model.py's docstring — input 'frame' 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output 'uvc' [[u, v, conf]] with u, v normalised map coords and conf in [0,1]; export via model.model.export_onnx unchanged. Training reads only buckets(meta, "train") via the existing load_scene() — nothing may open the truedop_2024 eval capture in any form. Keep all per-view work on the device and add no .item()/.cpu() host syncs inside the step loop. Keep weight averaging (start epoch, AVG_EVERY), BN recalibration, MixStyle, committee with independent augmentation draws per member, margin loss, augmentation, the bf16-autocast-on-CUDA path and the LR schedule exactly as they are. Run a quick syntax/import check (`python -c 'import model.train'`) and, if cheap, one tiny smoke step on CPU with max_chunks to confirm shapes (B divisible by n_caps, jsd finite) before finishing.
